title: What Are You Beholding?
headline: Why Self-Examination Isn’t Enough
tagline: Diagnosis can tell you where the wound is. Diagnosis cannot become the healer.
seo_title: Why Self-Examination Isn't Enough: Beholding Christ (2 Cor. 3:18) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: You can become so skilled at examining yourself that you become the main object of your own attention. A devotional for men on 2 Corinthians 3:18.
verse_text: And we all, who with unveiled faces contemplate the Lord’s glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

scriptures.text: And we all, who with unveiled faces contemplate the Lord’s glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
Fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith….
Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.

items: In this series, we have asked many questions.

blocks.text: You can become so skilled at examining yourself that you become the primary object of your own attention.

items: Eventually discipleship has to lift our eyes.
Paul gives us something much greater: behold.
Spiritual formation is not merely about what we stop looking at.
It also involves where we learn to look.

blocks.text: “If I understand myself deeply enough, I can transform myself.”

items: Knowing why you are bitter does not automatically produce forgiveness.
Knowing why you control does not automatically produce trust.
Knowing why you seek approval does not automatically establish identity.
Knowing why you fear does not automatically produce courage.
Diagnosis can tell you where the wound is.
The framework is a flashlight. It is not the Light.
Faith does not require smaller problems. It requires a larger frame.
The deepest answer to lesser fascination is not always greater willpower. Sometimes it is greater vision.
Diagnosis serves return. And return eventually teaches the eyes where to look.
